The most advanced statewide effort is in New York, but none of the search results confirm whether it has become law.

- **New York:** Both chambers passed the Responsible Data Center Development Act in early June 2026, which would pause state permits for large data centers for one year. The bill cleared the Senate 44–16 and the Assembly 102-39 on June 4, 2026. If Governor Kathy Hochul signs it, New York would become the first state to enact a statewide data center moratorium. Hochul had not taken a position in the sources I found, and they are dated only through early July.
- **Maine:** The legislature passed a statewide moratorium in April 2026, but Maine's Democratic governor vetoed what would have been the country's first state moratorium on the construction of data centers. Maine Governor Mills signed an executive order on 29 April, the same day the veto override attempt of the state moratorium bill failed, creating an advisory council.
- **Other states:** State lawmakers in at least 14 states have attempted to pass various forms of data center construction moratoriums in 2026, but none have succeeded. South Dakota's one-year moratorium bill failed in a state Senate committee amid opposition from power plant owners and data center developers. Vermont and Wisconsin also had bills introduced, per the sources.
- **Context:** No US state has enacted a permanent ban on data centers as of May 2026.
